L73: # Canine Cancer: Mast cell tumor
L74: 
L75: We are conducting a study on canine mast cell tumors to evaluate their cells and their response to specific chemotherapy drugs.
L76: 
L77: 【33†Image: Veterinary Technician caring for french terrier dog†cdn.prod.website-files.com】
L78: 
L79: ## 01.
L80: Brief Summary
L81: 
L82: Enrollment on hold (January 2026)
L83: 
L84: ImpriMed is actively conducting research on canine mast cell tumors (MCT). With your help, we can develop new precision oncology solutions to help you optimize treatment of this disease.
L85: ## 02.
L86: Benefits per case
L87: 
L88: 【34†Image†cdn.prod.website-files.com】
L89: 
L90: benefits to clinic
L91: 
L92: 【35†Image†cdn.prod.website-files.com】
L93: 
L94: c-Kit exons 8 and 11 mutation testing, as well as the results from our exploratory flow cytometric panel, will be provided free of charge. (【36†Download sample report†cdn.prod.website-files.com】)
L95: 
L96: 【35†Image†cdn.prod.website-files.com】
L97: 
L98: Blood chemistry data will be provided.
L99: 
L100: 【35†Image†cdn.prod.website-files.com】
L101: 1 to 2 weeks after sample collection, we will request the patient’s medical record (including the cytology report) to records@imprimedicine.com. In return, we will send a $30 gift card for each complete medical record we receive.
L102: 
L103: 【35†Image†cdn.prod.website-files.com】
L104: 
L105: Another $10 gift card will be issued for every updated patient record received at records@imprimedicine.com.
L106: ## 03.
L107: Patient type
L108: 
L109: We are requesting the samples from:
L110: 
L111: 【37†Image†cdn.prod.website-files.com】
L112: 
L113: Canine patients with suspected mast cell tumors
L114: ## 04.
L115: Sample requirements
L116: 
L117: For each patient, we request all of the following:
L118: 
L119: 【35†Image†cdn.prod.website-files.com】
L120: 
L121: Solid tumor (~0.5cm^{3}) or FNA (10 million cells). We accept FNA samples of both resectable and non-resectable tumors. We ask that an FNA sample be taken within 15 minutes following resection.
L122: 
L123: 【35†Image†cdn.prod.website-files.com】
L124: 
L125: A copy of the cytology report (or how the diagnosis was confirmed)
L126: 
L127: 【35†Image†cdn.prod.website-files.com】
L128: Whole blood (2 mL; from jugular or peripheral venous venipuncture)
L129: 
L130: 【35†Image†cdn.prod.website-files.com】
L131: 
L132: Serum (> 0.6 mL)
L133: ## 05.
L134: Sample Submission
L135: 
L136: If you have not already, please register for access to our 【38†Vet Portal by clicking here】. To submit sample information, go to ‘Sample Submission’ > Canine Services, and select 'Canine MCT Pilot Study'
L137: 
L138: Please ensure all participating pet owners sign the 【39†consent form†cdn.prod.website-files.com】 to allow us to use their dog’s sample for research.
L139: ## Sign up Here
L140: 
L141: To get started, fill out the form and we will send you our proprietary transport media tubes to your clinic.
L142:

L72: Flow Cytometry + PARR for Feline Lymphoma & Leukemia
L73: # Immunoprofile
L74: 
L75: The ImpriMed Immunoprofile report includes both our complete PARR and flow cytometry testing, as well as an expert interpretation of the results. This combined service includes cell size, clonality, and immunophenotype information that supports an accurate diagnosis of lymphoma and leukemia.
L76: 
L77: 【33†Image†cdn.prod.website-files.com】
L78: 
L79: ## Get cell sizing and immunophenotyping information in 3-4 calendar days*
L80: ### What's included:
L81: 
L82: 【34†Image†cdn.prod.website-files.com】
L83: 
L84: 1. PARR (PCR for Antigen Receptor Rearrangement) assay is used to test for B-cell or T-cell clonality, and high-specificity detection of the presence of neoplasia.
L85: 
L86: 【35†Image†cdn.prod.website-files.com】
L87: 
L88: 2. Flow cytometry
L89: Flow cytometry provides cell-sizing information and analyzes different proteins found on and within tumor cells that denotes immunophenotype. This test provides prognostic information for leukemia and lymphoma.
L90: 【36†Image†cdn.prod.website-files.com】
L91: 
L92: [Complimentary for a limited time] AI-driven Chlorambucil/CHOP Prognostication
L93: Our AI-driven predictions tell you if your patient is at low or high risk for early disease progression when treated with Chlorambucil/Prednisolone or CHOP combination therapy, and provides an estimate of the time until disease progression.
L94: 
L95: Sample Collection
L96: 
L97: 【37†Image†cdn.prod.website-files.com】
L98: For Lymphoma: Collect a biopsy (FNA or tissue) from the affected site(s) into ImpriMed transport tubes. Additionally, collect 2 mL of whole blood in an EDTA-treated tube.
L99: 
L100: 【37†Image†cdn.prod.website-files.com】
L101: 
L102: For Leukemia: Collect 2 mL of whole blood in an EDTA-treated tube.
L103: 
L104: *After the receipt of the sample at the lab in California
L105: 
L106: 【38†Image: Cat with a question mark†cdn.prod.website-files.com】
L107: ## Why should I order the Immunoprofile service instead of stand-alone PARR or Flow Cytometry?
L108: 
L109: The two tests provide complimentary and different information. PARR has high specificity but lower sensitivity. Flow cytometry has high sensitivity and specificity, but does not enable discrimination between neoplasia and reactive conditions. Together, the two tests enable a more accurate diagnosis.
L110: 
L111: *After the receipt of the sample at the lab in California
L112: ## How Does ImpriMed Use Flow Cytometry for cell sizing
L113: For the correct classification of feline lymphoma, two critical factors are paramount: the anatomic form and the size of the lymphocytes. Our new Feline lymphoma/leukemia services enrich your patient care by integrating immunophenotyping and, importantly, precise cell sizing through flow cytometry.
L114: We have developed a novel cell sizing technique using our expertise in flow cytometry and our extensive database of medical records with cytology/histology results from our feline lymphoma research efforts. Flow cytometry is a powerful tool to determine phenotype, cell granularity, and relative cell size. Our method leverages a comprehensive database of medical records and research findings.
L115: By comparing flow cytometry results with traditional gold standards (cytology or histology) used in these records, we have defined a method to assess lymphoma cells as small, medium, or large. This approach accurately categorizes lymphocyte size, as validated with an inter-laboratory comparison of our flow cytometry sizing and cytology provided by an accredited diagnostics laboratory.
L116: Our novel cell sizing system for feline lymphoma provides an accurate and reproducible readout of this important characterization parameter for your patient’s lymphocytes.
L117: 【39†Image: A male scientist looking through a microscope†cdn.prod.website-files.com】

L98: # Clinical research trials
L99: 
L100: Volunteers make our game-changing research possible.
L101: 
L102: We regularly require animals (and sometimes humans!) for our research studies.
L103: 
L104: See below for current research trials seeking volunteers.
L105: ## Dog cancer research trial
L106: 
L107: University of Queensland veterinary researchers are recruiting pet dogs diagnosed with cancer to test an experimental vaccine.
L108: 
L109: The clinical research trial is for dogs recently diagnosed with canine appendicular osteosarcoma, a common bone tumour that affects 10,000 dogs a year globally.
L110: 
L111: 【43†Take part in the trial†survey.app.uq.edu.au】
L112: ## Labrador and Golden Retriever overweight research project
L113: 
L114: University of Queensland veterinary researchers are investigating how obesity and being overweight affects the health and happiness of dogs, focusing on metabolism, gut health, body fat distribution and brain function.
L115: 
L116: Your participation could help us understand these connections better and help prevent and manage this condition in the future.
L117:

L9: # Register your interest in our dog cancer trial
L10: 
L11: We are recruiting dogs with mast cell cancer in Australia for an investigational trial of personalised mRNA cancer vaccines. Register your interest and share a few details about your dog. Our team will contact you about further screening.
L12: 
L13: 【5†Register your interest  →】 【8†See how it works  →】
L14: 
L15: Why we are running this trial
L16: ## From Rosie’s story to a future for more dogs.
L17: 
L18: 【9†Image: Rosie】
L19: 
L20: Rosie
L21: 
L22: The first dog treated with a personalised neoantigen vaccine.
L23: 
L24: It began with Rosie. Her experience with a personalised neoantigen vaccine encouraged Paul to explore how this approach could one day be made available to every dog with cancer.
L25: Before an approach like this can become broadly available, we must study it carefully and support it by evidence for review by the relevant veterinary regulators. This clinical trial is an important step in that process, helping us learn from participating dogs and understand the vaccine more fully.
L26: 
L27: 【2†Read Rosie’s personalised mRNA cancer-vaccine story  →】
L28: 
L29: Who can register
L30: ## If your dog has cancer and is currently in Australia, you’re welcome to register your interest. Our team will check whether your dog may be eligible for this trial.
L31:

L34: About the trial
L35: 
L36: ## What this trial is looking at
L37: 
L38: The trial will investigate a personalised mRNA vaccine approach for dogs with mast cell cancer. Tell us about your dog and our team will help determine whether they may be eligible for screening.
L39: 
L40: 【10†Image】
L41: ### Who can register
L42: 
L43: Dogs diagnosed with mast cell cancer who are based in, or able to travel within, Australia.
L44: 
L45: Every case is reviewed individually
L46: 
L47: 【11†Image】
L48: 
L49: ### The trial approach
L50: 
L51: A therapeutic mRNA vaccine designed from each dog’s own tumour and blood samples, intended to work alongside—not replace—existing care.
L52: 
L53: Personalised to each dog
L54: 
L55: 【12†Image】
L56: ### What screening involves
L57: 
L58: We help coordinate records, screening, sample logistics and updates, working with the trial team and your treating veterinarian.
L59: 
L60: A named team stays in touch
L61: 
L62: Trial registration and screening
L63: 
L64: ## How to register your interest.
L65: 
L66: You don’t need to have every record ready before registering your interest. Start with what you know and we’ll help with the rest.
L67: 
L68: 01
L69: ### Register your interest
L70: 
L71: Complete a short form with basic details about your dog, their mast cell cancer diagnosis and where you live.
L72: 
L73: 02
L74: 
L75: ### We get in touch
L76: 
L77: A Gamgee coordinator will contact you, answer practical questions and—with your permission—help gather relevant records from your vet.

L80: ### The trial team confirms eligibility
L81: 
L82: The authorised study team and treating veterinarian assess potential eligibility. If your dog may proceed, you’ll receive the approved trial information and consent discussion before deciding.
